decisions.reason: The existing message-595 MODIFY already states that every successful primary mint generates one commission and ticket, assigns no-code or invalid-code rewards randomly, and excludes secondary-market sales.

The existing message-595 MODIFY already updates the prize-pool copy to cover one ticket per successful primary mint, random assignment for no-code or invalid-code mints, and exclusion of secondary sales; the remaining mission copy stays valid.
The existing message-595 MODIFY already includes tickets from all successful primary mints, including randomly allocated tickets, while excluding secondary-market sales.

The existing message-595 MODIFY already establishes one Small Block ticket per successful primary mint and removes the obsolete referral-only issuance key; the pre-existing state already excludes secondary sales and includes no-code or invalid-code mints.
The existing message-595 MODIFY already establishes one randomly allocated $5 commission and one Small Block ticket per successful primary mint, excluding secondary-market sales.
The source concerns commission and ticket issuance cardinality and random allocation, not prize payout, collection, or winner-notification behavior.
The hero's statement that referrals earn a commission and ticket remains valid; the source does not require the concise hero copy to enumerate no-code, invalid-code, or secondary-sale rules.
The source does not change fiat-buyer wallet provisioning, wallet assets, dashboard access, SIWE access, or cash-out guidance.
The ticket and commission allocation rule does not change the Transak provider, supported payment methods, fiat conversion, or NFT fulfillment flow.
The source does not mention or logically change email delivery, confirmation contents, winner notifications, or reward guidance emails.
The current allocation already assigns one $5 referral commission per primary mint; the source concerns registration and recipient assignment for randomly distributed rewards, not the monetary split.
The source has no effect on the landing-page book cover's location, size, cropping, overlap, or visibility rules.
